summary: Added a separate opt-in bounded_consistent_hashing Model Gateway policy. Explicit X-SMG-Routing-Key requests retain their consistent-hash preference unless both the configured absolute active-request gap and relative max_load_skew bound are exceeded, then spill to the first eligible healthy worker clockwise on the cached ring. Strict consistent_hashing, X-SMG-Target-Worker, implicit authorization/forwarded-for/cookie affinity, one-worker behavior, and no-eligible-candidate behavior remain strict/safe. Added metrics, standalone and Python configuration surfaces, full HTTP request-lifetime load tracking, and a cached aggregate non-IGW regular-HTTP ring.

tests.what_was_measured: Rust formatting for the complete gateway workspace.

18 bounded-policy/config/router tests: below-bound affinity, absolute-plus-relative spill threshold, deterministic clockwise spill, implicit-key strictness, target-worker strictness, unhealthy failover/recovery, one/no-worker behavior, missing-ring fallback, near-idle adversarial vectors, candidate gap placement, and request-load tracking.
32 matching tests, including the unchanged strict consistent-hashing behavior and explicit load-invariance regression.
8 native tests covering streaming completion, client disconnect/drop, non-streaming upstream body reads, empty bodies, multiple guards, and explicit routing-key load lifetime.
A real Router-to-two-HTTP-worker integration regression proving spill follows key-relative clockwise ring order in non-IGW mode.
Full native gateway library regression suite: 415 passed.
All Rust library, binary, test, example, and benchmark targets against the privately generated resolution lock.
Rebuilt native PyO3 extension and source Python package: 100 passed, 1 skipped; validates enum conversion, CLI choices and threshold propagation.
The newly built standalone native binary advertises the policy and both configuration knobs.

tests.command: Initial source/interpreter path Python tests before rebuilding and selecting the checkout extension
tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before compatibility evidence: the preinstalled gateway rejected bounded_consistent_hashing and lacked PolicyType.BoundedConsistentHashing; after the native rebuild and explicit checkout path, the same tests passed.

gpu_execution.evidence: No GPU kernels or model numerical outputs are changed by this Rust HTTP routing feature. No model-backed GPU benchmark was run; CPU-native policy tests and a real two-worker HTTP transport regression cover the implementation boundary.

remaining_limitations: Worker::load() is an active-request counter local to one gateway process; separate gateway replicas can make different best-effort spill decisions.

Spillover sacrifices backend-local KV/cache locality and is unsafe when routing-key affinity is an application correctness requirement; those clients must use strict consistent_hashing or X-SMG-Target-Worker.

The model-backed two-worker GPU A/B benchmark requested as suggested validation was not rerun in this job. Therefore this contribution makes no new throughput, p95 latency, cache-hit, prefill-work, semantic-accuracy, model-architecture, or distributed-workload claim.

The repository did not contain a checked-in sgl-model-gateway/Cargo.lock. The first --locked attempt therefore failed before compilation; dependency resolution was generated privately for the subsequent locked all-target check and was not added to the contribution.

The prepared image initially lacked cargo despite rust-toolchain.toml pinning Rust 1.90. Rust 1.90 and build caches were installed only under /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-67f607c4b6ab; node-wide Torch/ROCm and host state were not changed.
